import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [tuple(fp) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        h = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.type_heads):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([h, mx, av], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 40
N_RES = 3


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)

        g = self.glob(torch.cat([x.mean((2, 3)), x.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

VOX_W = 16
WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.conv3d = nn.Conv3d(8, VOX_W, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2d = nn.Conv2d(VOX_W * spec.Z, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        vox = torch.stack([obs[:, 0:Z], obs[:, Z:2 * Z], obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]], dim=1)
        scal = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        v = torch.cat([vox, scal, zc], dim=1)
        v = F.relu(self.conv3d(v))
        f = v.reshape(B, -1, Y, X)
        f = F.relu(self.conv2d(f))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
PROJ = 32
HID = 24


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [tuple(fp) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(4 * PROJ, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        h = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.type_heads):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([h, mx, mn, av], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 40
N_RES = 3


class ChanLN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):

        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(c)

        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [tuple(fp) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.stem_ln = ChanLN(WIDTH)
        self.res = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(N_RES)])

        g = self.glob(torch.cat([x.mean((2, 3)), x.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HEADS = 4


class ChanLN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(c)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.ln(x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [tuple(fp) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), ChanLN(WIDTH), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), ChanLN(WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, spec.Y * spec.X, WIDTH) * 0.02)
        self.attn_ln = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(WIDTH, HEADS, batch_first=True)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        B, W, Y, X = f.shape
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos
        a = self.attn_ln(t)
        a = self.attn(a, a, a, need_weights=False)[0]
        t = t + a
        f = t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, W, Y, X)
        h = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.type_heads):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([h, mx, av], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: LN in footprint-head projection
trials.hypothesis: Change: r2c3 with a per-cell channel LayerNorm before the ReLU in the head's 1x1 projection, which feeds the footprint pooling. Why: LayerNorm in the body gave the best and most stable runs. Normalising the pooled head features too should keep the scale of placement logits steady early on, so fewer seeds collapse. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is not above 0.83 or the seed gap grows beyond 0.05.
trials.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64


class ChanLN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(c)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.ln(x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [tuple(fp) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), ChanLN(WIDTH), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), ChanLN(WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 1), ChanLN(WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        h = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.type_heads):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([h, mx, av], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: No trials yet. The starting network scores between 0.16 and 0.54 depending on the seed (4-seed mean 0.345), so a single 2-seed mean is only trustworthy for gaps of roughly 0.15 or more. What the agent needs to see is mostly local. For each brick type and anchor it needs the landing layer, which is the highest build cell under the footprint, and whether the target is missing cells across the whole footprint at that layer. It also needs order: lower cells must go in before overhangs seal them. A bigger network trains for fewer steps, so I keep every candidate's compute close to the start (about 1.0 to 1.3x). This round tests three ideas: (1) a placement head that sees the whole footprint, since the start's 1x1 head scores only the anchor cell; (2) a deeper, narrower residual body with global context at the same compute; (3) a 3D voxel encoder that treats layers explicitly, which should make landing layers and overhangs easier to learn.
analyses.2: Pooling the head over each brick's footprint (r1c1) gave 0.67, with both seeds (0.81, 0.53) at or above the starting architecture's best seed. That is the clearest gain so far, though the seed spread is still large. The deeper residual body with global context (r1c2) scored 0.52, but its seeds were split (0.32, 0.72), so it may help and needs confirming. The 3D voxel encoder failed on both seeds (0.10 each), so I am dropping it. A placement is correct only if, at the brick's landing layer (the highest filled cell under its footprint), every footprint cell is missing in the build. A linear head over pooled features cannot easily express that 'every cell at this layer' condition. A head with a hidden layer and min-pooling should handle it better. Seed-to-seed failure is the main risk, so I also test normalisation as a way to make training more stable.
analyses.3: The footprint-pooled placement head is the clear win. It raised the mean from 0.35 to 0.67 on its own, and both later variants built on it scored above 0.80 with tight seed pairs: r2c1 got 0.79 and 0.82, r2c3 got 0.84 and 0.82. Two body changes both helped on top of this head: a deeper residual body with a global vector (r2c1, 0.805) and channel LayerNorm (r2c3, 0.830). With only 2 seeds per trial, these two are statistically tied. Two ideas failed: the 3D voxel encoder (0.10, which looks like collapse) and a heavier min/max/mean head with a hidden layer (0.35). The heavier head cost about 1.3x compute and may also have made optimisation harder. So keep the head linear and the compute near 1.1x. Next: combine LayerNorm with the residual body, give the placement head global context, and test one cheap self-attention layer for long-range ordering.
analyses.4: The footprint-pooled head is the one big win: 0.35 rose to 0.67, and to 0.80–0.83 once it sat on a better body. Per-cell LayerNorm in r2c3 gave the best and most stable result (0.836 and 0.824). The residual body with a global vector (r2c1, 0.80) did about as well as r2c3. Putting the two together (r3c1, 0.78) did not add up. Adding global context into the head (r3c2) split the seeds badly. Ideas that cut training steps lost: attention at 1.46x compute and the hidden-layer min/max head at 1.31x. On an 8x8 grid, two 3x3 convs plus footprint pooling already see about 6x6 cells, so more receptive field probably matters little. The most promising changes are cheap ones that keep about 118k steps. One is sharper local information in the head, such as exact per-layer bits from obs. The others are normalisation in the head and depth through width rather than residual stacking. All three stay at about 1.1x compute.
